about: Ranking and "what this brings" notes for the Prompt Board. The order of ids across the tiers is the rank (most important first). Edit, then run node tools/gen-prompts.mjs.

tiers.title: Start here
tiers.blurb: The ones that keep the numbers you rely on right and your data safe, plus the gaps that matter most.

tiers.title: Next
tiers.blurb: Big improvements to pages you already use, and the core pages still missing.

tiers.title: Later
tiers.blurb: Useful additions you will reach for now and then.

value.heavy-federal-tax-grid: Checks the federal tax engine against 12,000 returns worked from the IRS's own rules, across every filing status, income mix and threshold for 2024 to 2026. Your tax estimate drives the retirement, withdrawal and Roth conversion advice, so a slip here quietly spreads to many other numbers.
value.quick-state-tax-tables: Puts every state's income tax rules (all 50 states and DC, 2025 and 2026) into the app as data, each figure from the state's own tax department. The State tax page cannot be built without it, and state tax is often thousands of dollars a year in every take-home and retirement figure.
value.heavy-golden-retirement: Builds thousands of hand-worked test cases for the main retirement pages: the year-by-year projection, contributions, withdrawals, Roth conversions, required withdrawals and more. These pages answer "will the money last?", the most important question in the app, so every formula behind it deserves an answer key.
value.heavy-social-security-grid: Checks the Social Security page against 2,000 invented work histories at every claiming age from 62 to 70, using the Social Security Administration's own rules. When to claim is one of the biggest retirement decisions, often worth tens of thousands of dollars, so the benefit figures must be exact.
value.build-taxes-state: Builds the State tax page, so your plan counts state income tax instead of guessing it. In most states that is thousands of dollars a year, and every retirement and take-home figure depends on it. Send it after the state tax tables prompt, which supplies the data it needs.
value.reasoning-monte-carlo-validation: Checks that the 'Chance the money lasts' page is statistically sound: the same starting number gives the same answer, zero randomness reproduces plain growth, the random returns have the right average and spread, and the result settles as runs increase. That percentage is the headline answer on whether your retirement money lasts.
value.audit-privacy: Re-reads the public repo as a stranger trying to work out who you are and what you own, and tries to slip text past your leak guard. Anything personal, even an indirect clue, is listed with its location. Once code is public it is hard to take back, so this protects your identity and money details.
value.swarm-retirement-validation: Re-creates six well-known results (the 4% rule study, the Trinity study, guardrail spending rules, required withdrawals, Social Security benefits and the random-returns simulation) with the planner's engine and explains every gap. You learn whether a difference is a documented choice or a bug before you rely on the engine's verdict.
value.heavy-golden-taxes: Builds thousands of hand-worked test cases for the other tax pages: brackets, capital gains, estimated payments, the multi-year tax projection, and health savings and spending accounts. Tax figures feed many decisions, so each of these pages needs its own answer key.
value.reasoning-security-review: Has a reviewer try to break into the PC server the way someone on your Wi-Fi, a malicious web page or a booby-trapped bank statement might, and rank what turns up, with fixes and tests. The server holds your whole financial plan, so closing a hole here protects your most private data.
value.reasoning-planning-methodology: Has an expert-style review of the retirement method: default return and inflation assumptions, taxes, withdrawal rules, shifting from stocks to bonds over time, and what a careful planner would add next, ranked by how much each could change a decision. The top three gaps come with fixes, so the advice you rely on rests on firmer ground.
value.build-goals-emergency-fund: Builds the Emergency fund page: how many months of bills your cash covers, and how much to set aside each month to reach your target. It is the first safety net in almost every financial plan.
value.quick-rmd-tables: Checks the required withdrawals page against IRS tables and adds missing cases: the table for a spouse more than ten years younger, inherited accounts, start ages by birth date, and the first-year April deadline that can force two withdrawals in one year. Mistakes here mean a missed withdrawal, a tax penalty or a tax surprise.
value.build-retirement-pensions: Builds the Pensions page, so your retirement plan counts a pension: the monthly benefit, cost-of-living increases and survivor options, plus lump sum versus monthly payments. Today the retirement pages have no way to include one, and a pension choice is usually permanent.
value.swarm-audit-all-math: Sends a team of AI workers through every working page's calculations, one group each, then re-checks every claimed error by hand and compares formulas that appear in more than one place. Disagreements between pages, such as two different payment formulas, surface. Each accepted fix comes with a test that fails before and passes after. It overlaps with the answer-key jobs: those test the numbers at volume, this one reads every formula against its source.
value.heavy-golden-debt: Builds thousands of hand-worked test cases for the payoff plan, mortgage, refinance, credit card and debt-ratio pages. Wrong numbers here mean wrong payoff dates, wrong interest totals and a wrong call on whether refinancing pays.
value.build-retirement-medicare: Builds the Medicare and IRMAA page, showing what Medicare's premiums for doctor visits (Part B) and prescriptions (Part D) cost at your income, plus the income surcharge (IRMAA) that raises them for higher earners. These come out of retirement income, and a big income year can raise them two years later.
value.quick-server-tests: Adds automated tests that start your PC server and check its safety rules: your settings file and data folder are never served, the access token is enforced, and a saved plan comes back intact with a backup made. If a later change weakens a rule, a test fails instead of your data leaking.
value.heavy-loan-schedules: Checks the loan math behind every debt page against 20,000 loans worked to the cent, including extra payments, lump sums, biweekly plans and recasts. Wrong schedules mean wrong payoff dates and wrong "what an extra $100 saves" answers when you decide which debt to attack first.
value.heavy-retirement-replays: Replays every retirement start year since 1871 for every withdrawal rate, stock mix and length of retirement, and checks the historical page against it. That page answers "would my plan have survived the worst real years?", which is how you judge whether your spending is safe. It overlaps with the check against published retirement studies: that one explains the famous results, this one covers every case.
value.swarm-tax-vs-irs-worksheets: Compares the federal tax engine with the IRS's own worksheets for 2024 to 2026, one worker per form: rates, investment gains, tax on Social Security benefits, child credit, extra investment taxes and the 2025 law changes. Agreements become tests, gaps become fixes, and the page gains a plain 'what this covers' table. It overlaps with the 12,000-return federal answer key: run that one first; this one adds the form-by-form diagnosis.
value.build-scenarios-advisor-plan: Builds the Advisor's plan page, where you enter an advisor's assumptions and recommendations as a scenario and compare them with your own plan. You can see which assumptions explain any difference between the two sets of results.
value.heavy-state-tax-grid: Builds an answer key for state income tax in all 50 states and DC, so the State tax page can be proven right the day it is built. State tax is often thousands of dollars a year, and every take-home and retirement figure will lean on it. Most useful once the State tax page exists.
value.heavy-households-verify: Works out by hand the key figures for the 1,400 pretend households the tester uses, and sorts every mismatch into an app bug or a wrong expectation. It turns a pile of failing test cases into a short list of real fixes across net worth, spending, debt and goals.
value.research-withdrawal-research: Summarises safe-withdrawal and market-return research since 2023 (Morningstar, guardrail updates, large firms' ten-year forecasts) and says which of the planner's default assumptions and withdrawal methods are now out of line, with fixes. Those defaults quietly drive every retirement answer, so keeping them current protects the headline result.
value.quick-csv-hardening: Makes the importer read the odd layouts real banks produce: semicolon-separated files, European-style decimals, amounts in brackets or marked credit and debit, and different date orders. Fewer files get refused or misread, so your imported spending and income come out right the first time.
value.quick-life-tables: Replaces the rough curve behind 'How long to plan for' with the Social Security Administration's real life table, and measures how far the old curve was off at each age. The age your plan must last to is a major input to whether the money runs out, so this makes that input better grounded.
value.heavy-golden-basics: Builds thousands of hand-worked test cases for the net worth, cash cushion, debts list, household, goals and assumptions pages. These are the numbers you see first, and an answer key keeps them right as the app keeps changing.
value.heavy-golden-cashflow: Builds thousands of hand-worked test cases for the income, expenses, budget, bills, forecast and spending pages. Your monthly picture rests on these sums, so a slip here makes your budget and forecast quietly wrong.
value.build-system-backups: Builds the Backups page, which lists the saved copies of your plan on the server, shows what changed between them and lets you restore any one. If a mistake or a bad sync overwrites your numbers, you can bring the earlier version back.
value.heavy-golden-investments: Builds thousands of hand-worked test cases for the investment pages: allocation, rebalancing, fees, performance, dividends, risk, tax lots and more. It catches wrong fee costs, wrong returns or wrong trades before they mislead your investing decisions.
value.heavy-historical-data-audit: Compares every number in the app's historical market data (about 10,000 values going back to 1871) with the original published files. Several retirement and investment pages replay that history, so one typo there skews every "would this have lasted?" answer.
value.research-2025-tax-law: Lists every 2025 tax-law change that affects a household (senior deduction, state and local tax cap, tips, overtime, car-loan interest, child credit, estate exemption, 529 plans, new children's accounts) and compares it with what the tax page covers. You learn what the estimate gets right, what it ignores and roughly what ignoring it costs.
value.research-2027-figures: Finds the official 2027 numbers (tax brackets, deductions, retirement-account limits, Social Security and Medicare figures) and compares them with the planner's estimates, which are inflated guesses for now. Swapping guesses for published figures makes next year's tax and contribution numbers right, with a source beside each.
value.build-scenarios-compare: Builds the Scenario compare page: copy your plan, change a few things and see the key results side by side. You can try retiring earlier, saving more or buying a house without touching your real numbers.
value.build-retirement-healthcare: Builds the Healthcare before 65 page, showing what plans on the Affordable Care Act (ACA) marketplace cost at different incomes, the subsidy you would get and the income levels where that help drops sharply. If you stop work before Medicare starts at 65, this can be one of your largest costs.
value.quick-alerts-milestones: Adds reminders to Needs attention for age milestones in the next twelve months: 59½, 62, the Medicare sign-up window before 65, full retirement age for Social Security, and when required withdrawals start. Some of these dates carry penalties or lower benefits if missed, so an early nudge protects real money.
value.reasoning-ai-guardrails: Tightens the rules for the AI features: numbers the assistant quotes are checked against figures the app computed, rows read from statements pass a review step before reaching your plan, and less of your data is sent to the model. It keeps a confident but wrong answer from ending up in your numbers.
value.reasoning-established-dashboard: Redesigns the Dashboard for when your plan is already set up: the three or four numbers that matter (net worth and its change, this month's spending against plan, the retirement verdict, the next action), the Needs attention count and what changed since your last visit. It is the screen you see every time you open the app.
value.audit-test-gaps: Finds the calculations that have no test, and the cases never exercised (zero balances, missing dates, negative inputs), ranks them by how big a number they affect on screen, and writes tests for the top twenty. Any hidden bug it exposes is flagged first. Untested formulas are where wrong numbers hide.
value.build-overview-next-best-action: Builds the Next best action page, which tells you where your next spare dollar should go: employer match first, then high-interest debt, an emergency fund, retirement and the rest. It turns a pile of numbers into one clear step, which is what most people need when there is money left over.
value.quick-empty-plan-sweep: Runs every page's calculations on an empty plan, the sample plans and plans filled with odd numbers (zero, negative, huge, missing), and checks that nothing crashes or shows 'not a number' or infinite results. It catches broken pages before you do, and keeps catching them as pages are added.
value.reasoning-live-sync: Stops two devices from silently overwriting each other's changes. The server would refuse a save made from an out-of-date copy and tell you in plain words, and phones would pick up changes made elsewhere. Today the last save wins, so an entry made on one device can quietly vanish when another device saves.
value.reasoning-scenarios-engine: Builds the foundation for what-if scenarios: change a few things on a copy of your plan, then see net worth, retirement success, lifetime tax and debt-free date side by side with the original, without duplicating your data. It lets you test a decision, such as retiring a year earlier, before you make it.
value.quick-ofx-import: Lets you load the .ofx and .qfx files many banks offer, not only spreadsheet downloads. The bank's own transaction numbers help the app skip lines you already imported, so bringing in transactions takes fewer steps and your spending numbers stay current with less effort.
value.quick-health-cost-tables: Supplies the tables two planned pages need: marketplace health-plan subsidies before 65 (poverty guidelines and subsidy percentages) and Medicare premiums with the income-related surcharge (IRMAA) for 2024 to 2027, each sourced and tested. Healthcare is a big retirement cost, and these tables show where a little extra income raises it sharply.
value.heavy-spreadsheet-parity: Makes the app's payment, growth and return calculators give the same answers Excel does, across 10,000 cases including the awkward ones. When you check a number in a spreadsheet, it will match, and a quiet mismatch in these basics would ripple into loans, savings and returns.
value.swarm-phase8-protection-estate: Builds the insurance and estate pages in one go: policies, life insurance needs, term versus permanent, disability, estate documents, beneficiaries, legacy goals and gifting, all sharing one set of data. It fills the protection side of your plan, where gaps such as a wrong beneficiary only show up when it is too late.
value.research-bank-export-formats: Documents what the downloads from twenty large US banks, card issuers and brokerages really look like, adds a sample file for each, and fixes the importer wherever a format would be misread. Your own bank is then more likely to import correctly the first time, with signs and dates read the right way round.
value.build-scenarios-stress-tests: Builds the Stress tests page, which runs your plan through a market crash, job loss, an inflation spike, disability or the death of a spouse. You see how well the plan holds up to a bad event before one happens.
value.build-taxes-self-employment: Builds the Self-employment page, which works out self-employment tax (Social Security and Medicare on your own earnings), the small-business deduction and other deductions on side income. Today the federal estimate leaves that tax out, so it can understate what you would owe.
value.quick-payee-cleanup: Teaches the app to turn bank text such as 'SQ *COFFEE 0421' or 'AMZN Mktp US*2K3AB1' into a clean merchant name, for thirty common patterns. The same shop is recognised month after month, so rules file more transactions automatically and Bills, Subscriptions and the cash forecast group payments better.
value.build-scenarios-goal-seek: Builds the Goal seek page, which works out what one thing, such as your savings rate, retirement age or investment return, would need to be to hit a target. It answers 'what would it take?' directly instead of by trial and error.
value.build-system-devices: Builds the Devices page, which names each phone or computer allowed into the app, lets you cut one off if it is lost, and can limit a device to viewing only. Your plan holds everything about your money, so locking out a lost phone matters.
value.build-debt-student-loans: Builds the Student loans page, which compares the standard repayment plan with plans that tie your payment to your income, and shows when any remaining balance could be forgiven. The plan you pick changes both your monthly payment and the total you repay.
value.heavy-golden-transactions: Builds thousands of test cases for importing, sorting, matching transfers and finding duplicates in your bank transactions. Mistakes here double-count or miss spending, which then flows into every budget and spending number.
value.reasoning-next-best-action: Builds the Next best action page: from your plan it tells you the next one to three things to do with a spare dollar, in the commonly taught order (employer match, high-interest debt, emergency fund, retirement saving), each with the reason in plain words. It turns many pages of numbers into one clear next step.
value.build-cashflow-paycheck: Builds the Paycheck page, which follows your pay from the gross amount to what reaches your bank: income tax withheld, Social Security and Medicare taxes, pre-tax deductions and employer match. You see where each dollar goes and whether you are leaving match money unclaimed.
value.build-insurance-life-needs: Builds the Life insurance needs page: how much coverage you need by two common methods, DIME (debts, income, mortgage, education) and the value of the earnings you would have made, compared with the coverage you have. It shows whether your family would be protected if you died.
value.reasoning-chart-kit: Creates one small shared chart toolkit and uses it on Net worth (history), Expenses (shares), Goals (progress) and Debts (payoff timeline). Charts exist today in three places with three looks, and most pages are still numbers and tables; pictures make trends and progress visible at a glance on a phone.
value.research-aca-subsidies: Establishes the current rules for marketplace health insurance before Medicare: what happened to the extra subsidies, the income cliff, which income counts and how retirees can manage it. It rewrites the Healthcare before 65 page's formulas so it can be built. If you retire before 65, your income choices could swing premiums by thousands.
value.build-estate-beneficiaries: Builds the Beneficiary audit page, which lists the primary and backup beneficiaries on every account and flags any that are missing or out of date. Beneficiary forms override your will, so an old or missing name can send money to the wrong person.
value.build-insurance-policies: Builds the Policies page, a list of every insurance policy you hold with its type, benefit, premium, term, insurer and renewal date. It puts your protection in one place, and the other insurance pages use it to find gaps.
value.build-overview-monthly-review: Builds the Monthly review page, a short walk through your month: spending against budget, the change in net worth, goal progress and your to-dos. A ten-minute check each month catches small problems before they grow.
value.build-reports-plan-summary: Builds the Plan summary page, a printable overview in the style of an advisor's plan: where you stand, your goals, your protection and your next steps. It is one document you can print, keep or take to a meeting.
value.quick-contribution-limits: Extends the table of yearly retirement-account limits (401(k), IRA, Roth, health savings, self-employed plans, catch-ups) from 2015 to 2027, each with its IRS source, including the 2026 rule that some catch-ups must go to a Roth account. The contribution pages then show the right room left, so you neither miss out nor overfund and risk a penalty.
value.quick-recurring-cadences: Tightens how the Bills page spots recurring payments: every four weeks versus monthly, month-end bills, bills that shift to the next business day, and yearly bills seen only twice, all tested with dates a few days off and a missed payment. Fewer real bills slip through, so your cash forecast and missed-payment warnings are more reliable.
value.reasoning-large-plans: Prepares the app for years of imported transactions: it measures how slow things get at 50,000 transactions, moves the browser's saved copy to a bigger storage area, and speeds up the slowest pages. Without it, a big history could fill the browser's storage and make pages sluggish.
value.build-ai-reader: Builds the Document reader page, which reads statements, pay stubs and an advisor's plan PDF and turns them into entries you can accept or reject. It saves typing, and nothing enters your plan until you approve it.
value.build-balance-projection: Builds the Net worth projection page, which shows your net worth 1 to 40 years ahead from your saving, investment returns and debt payoff. You see where today's habits lead while there is still time to change course.
value.build-goals-prioritizer: Builds the Goal prioritiser page, which splits your monthly surplus across your goals by priority and deadline. When there is not enough for everything, it shows which goals get funded first and which slip, so the trade-off is clear.
value.build-transactions-reconcile: Builds the Reconcile page, which compares a statement's ending balance with your ledger and helps you find what explains any gap. It catches missing, doubled or wrong transactions, so your spending reports rest on numbers you can trust.
value.audit-licences: Checks that every table, data set and software library the repo borrowed may be shared under its MIT licence, and adds a NOTICE file crediting each source. Now that the repo is public, this keeps you clear of licence complaints and credits the people whose work you build on.
value.reasoning-plain-words: Sweeps every working page for jargon, long sentences and system-speak, and proposes plain replacements without changing what any number means. Spelled-out terms and shorter sentences make each page easier to understand at a glance on a phone, without looking anything up.
value.build-estate-documents: Builds the Documents checklist page, which tracks whether your will, trust, power of attorney, healthcare directive and guardianship papers are done and when each was last updated. Without them, a court may decide who acts for you or who raises your children.
value.build-goals-house: Builds the House down payment page, which works out your savings target from the price, down payment percentage and closing costs, and the date you will reach it. It turns 'someday' into a monthly amount and shows whether your timeline is realistic.
value.build-insurance-disability: Builds the Disability page, which shows the gap between your pay and what disability coverage would replace, the waiting period before it starts, and group versus individual plans. If illness stopped you working, you would lose the income your whole plan depends on.
value.quick-networth-since-line: Adds a small line chart of your saved net worth over time, and a green or red line under the Net worth tile showing how much it moved since your last saved total, with the percentage. Today the history is only a table, so it is hard to see at a glance whether you are gaining ground.
value.quick-search-aliases: Lets you find pages by typing the way you would ask a question, such as 'how much do I owe' or 'when can I retire'. Every working page gets a few plain-word phrases, so you spend less time hunting through a menu of more than 150 pages.
value.build-balance-accounts: Builds the Account detail page: each account's balance history, a way to check it against your statements, and room for notes. It helps you catch a wrong balance before it throws off your net worth and everything built on it.
value.build-insurance-term-vs-permanent: Builds the Term vs permanent page, which compares cheap term life insurance plus investing the difference against permanent coverage (whole or universal life), using the numbers in the policy's own illustration. It helps you see whether a costly permanent policy is worth what it charges.
value.quick-dates-edge-tests: Tests the date and pay-period math at its awkward edges: February 29 birthdays, month-end dates, years with 27 paydays and time-zone quirks that once made dates a day early. Any bug found gets fixed. Ages and pay periods feed retirement timing and income figures, so a one-day slip could move a milestone.
value.reasoning-architecture-review: Has a reviewer examine how the app is built and name the five problems most likely to hurt as it grows past 150 pages, with fixes for the top three. You see no new screen. It keeps future pages from slowing or breaking each other, so the app stays dependable as you add to it.
value.audit-dependencies: Reviews the few outside software packages the PC server relies on, mainly the PDF reader: known security warnings, what a booby-trapped PDF could do, and whether downloads are locked to exact versions and verified. You get fixes that make the server safer when it reads your statements.
value.build-insurance-cash-value: Builds the Cash-value model page, which works out the true yearly return on the savings part (cash value) of a permanent life policy and whether to keep the policy or cash it in. It shows what your premiums have actually earned so far.
value.build-insurance-health: Builds the Health plan compare page, which compares plans on premiums plus the out-of-pocket costs you would expect, and flags which plans allow a health savings account (HSA). The cheapest premium is often not the cheapest plan once you use it.
value.build-insurance-ltc: Builds the Long-term care page, showing the odds you will need long-term care, what it costs in your state, and whether to pay for it yourself or buy a policy. Care can often cost far more than normal living costs, and Medicare pays for little of it.
value.build-overview-health-score: Builds the Plan health score page: a score from 0 to 100 covering your emergency fund, debt, savings rate, insurance gaps and estate papers, with a plain explanation of what pulls it down. It gives you one number to track and a short list of what to fix first.
value.reasoning-data-model-v2: Redesigns how your plan is stored so it can handle split transactions, more than one currency, balance history and safer links between items, and converts every existing plan without losing a number. It prepares the app for things it cannot do cleanly today, but it is a risky change touching many pages.
value.reasoning-encryption-at-rest: Lets you protect the saved plan with a passphrase so the PC only ever stores scrambled data. Someone who copies your plan file or backups cannot read it. The trade-offs: a forgotten passphrase means the data is gone, and the heaviest calculations that run on the PC need a workaround.
value.audit-performance: Looks for what slows the app on a mid-range phone: how much loads at start, what happens after every save, and pages that recalculate other pages repeatedly. You get the three biggest speed-ups as code changes. Faster pages make checking your numbers on a phone less of a chore.
value.build-ai-explain: Builds the Explain this page button, added to every page: it sends the page's numbers to the AI and shows you a plain-language explanation. It helps you understand what the figures mean without a finance background.
value.build-goals-education: Builds the Education (529) page, which plans monthly contributions to a 529 college savings plan, allowing for tuition inflation and your state's tax deduction. College is one of the largest costs a family plans for, and starting early makes it far easier to fund.
value.build-reports-retirement: Builds the Retirement report page, which pulls your retirement projections, Social Security, withdrawal plan and chance of success into one report. It puts the most important results in one place you can review, print or share.
value.reasoning-first-run-flow: Designs the first ten minutes for someone new: a few plain questions, rough answers accepted, and a dashboard that shows only what is honestly known at each step. If you or anyone else starts a fresh plan, it gets from empty to useful quickly, without false precision.
value.reasoning-help-content: Writes help text for every page (what it does, how to read it, where its numbers come from, common questions) as one data file for the planned Help page and a '?' on each page. You can find out what a number means without leaving the page or asking someone.
value.research-state-changes: Lists every state that changed its income tax for 2026 or has a change scheduled for 2027, with the law, date and new figures, plus a 'changes to watch' note for the State tax page. Whoever builds that page then knows which states need two versions of their rules.
value.build-ai-critic: Builds the Plan critic page, which asks the AI to list the gaps and risks it sees in your plan, each linked to the page where you can fix it. It is a second opinion that can spot what you did not think to check.
value.build-taxes-filing-status: Builds the Filing status compare page, which compares filing jointly, filing separately and as head of household to see which costs you least. Joint filing costs least for many couples, but the check takes seconds and can save money in unusual cases.
value.build-career-benefits: Builds the Benefits elections page, which helps you choose at open enrolment: your 401(k) percentage, health savings account, employer stock plan and insurance picks. These yearly choices are easy to rush and can leave employer money on the table.
value.build-debt-consolidation: Builds the Consolidation page, which compares rolling your debts into one new loan against keeping each one as it is. You see the total interest and payoff date both ways, so you can tell whether one payment is truly cheaper or just simpler.
value.build-household-calendar: Builds the Money calendar page, which puts your bills, paydays, tax deadlines, open enrolment, required withdrawal dates and policy renewals on one calendar. Some missed dates cost real penalties, and seeing them together makes them hard to miss.
value.build-insurance-property: Builds the Auto, home, umbrella page, which checks whether your auto, home and umbrella (extra liability) coverage is enough for what you own and your net worth. The goal is that a lawsuit or disaster never costs more than your insurance pays.
value.build-overview-timeline: Builds the Life timeline page, which lays your ages, retirement, goals, mortgage payoff, Medicare start and required withdrawals on one line. Seeing the dates together shows which ones land in the same year and which you have not planned for yet.
value.build-reports-export: Builds the Export page, which sends any table in the app to a spreadsheet (xlsx or csv) or to a plain data file (JSON). Your numbers stay yours, and you can share them with an accountant or study them in another tool.
value.build-retirement-annuities: Builds the Annuities page, where you enter annuity quotes to see the guaranteed monthly income they would add and how that compares with bonds. It shows whether trading a lump sum for income that cannot run out fits your plan.
value.build-system-audit: Builds the Change log page, which shows what changed in your data, when it changed and which device made the change. If a number looks wrong, you can trace what changed it.
value.quick-glossary: Writes at least 120 plain-words definitions of the terms the app uses, each with a small example and the pages that use it. When you meet a word like 'bracket' or 'required withdrawals', you can read what it means in a couple of sentences instead of searching the web.
value.research-long-term-care-costs: Collects what home care, assisted living and nursing homes cost in each state, plus the odds of needing paid care and for how long, with sources. The planned Long-term care page can then show a real price tag for a risk that can drain savings late in life.
value.build-ai-glossary: Builds the Glossary page, which explains every financial term used in the app in plain words, with search. When you meet a term like IRMAA or sequence risk, you can look it up without leaving the app.
value.build-investments-employer-stock: Builds the Employer stock page, showing how much of your wealth is in your employer's stock, when your stock plans vest (become yours) and the risk that carries. If your paycheck and savings depend on one company, a bad year can hit both at once.
value.build-property-home: Builds the Home page, which tracks your home's value, your equity in it, what it costs to keep and how much you expect it to appreciate. For many households the house is the largest asset, so it shapes net worth and retirement options.
value.quick-format-locales: Tests how amounts and percentages are displayed, in US dollars and Mexican pesos, and fixes oddities: no '-$0', no 'NaN' (not a number) when a figure is missing, and consistent rounding of half-cents. Consistent, clean numbers on every page make the whole app easier to trust at a glance.
value.reasoning-empty-states: Gives each working page a short, friendly message when it has nothing to show yet: what the page will tell you, what it needs from you, and a button to start. Instead of empty tables and zeros, you know what to do first. It mostly helps when you start a new area.
value.build-cashflow-budget-percent: Builds the Budget (50/30/20) page, which splits your income into needs, wants and savings using the 50/30/20 rule or percentages you choose. It is a quick check that your spending is balanced, without tracking every envelope.
value.build-estate-legacy: Builds the Legacy goals page, where you record what you want to leave and to whom. That sets the amount your plan aims to have left at the end, which changes how much you can safely spend now.
value.build-goals-vehicle: Builds the Vehicle page, which helps you decide whether to save up for your next vehicle or finance it, and on what timeline. A vehicle is often one of your biggest purchases, so the choice affects your budget for years.
value.build-property-rent-vs-buy: Builds the Rent vs buy page, which compares the total cost of renting against buying over any number of years, counting what your money could earn elsewhere. It shows when buying pulls ahead and when renting wins.
value.build-reports-tax: Builds the Tax report page, which reports your tax picture for this year alongside the multi-year projection. It gives you something clear to hand to a tax preparer or to review before you file.
value.build-retirement-buckets: Builds the Bucket strategy page, which sizes cash, bond and stock buckets by how many years of spending each one needs to cover. It gives you a simple way to see that the next few years of spending are safe from a market drop.
value.build-scenarios-sensitivity: Builds the Sensitivity page, which ranks your assumptions by how much each one moves the result, in a bar chart. You see which guesses matter and which hardly do, so you know where to be careful.
value.build-system-help: Builds the Help page, which explains how the app works, with a section for every page. When you are unsure what a page does, or a family member has to use the app in an emergency, the answer is one tap away.
value.research-student-loans: Spells out federal student loan repayment after the 2025 law (the new repayment plan, what became of SAVE, income-based plans, forgiveness timing, public service forgiveness) with sources and five worked examples. It gives the planned Student loans page correct rules, which matters only if you or your family carry federal student loans.
value.audit-accessibility: Checks colour contrast in light and dark mode, keyboard use, screen-reader labels, charts and animation against the WCAG 2.2 AA web accessibility standard, and fixes the shared styles. Text becomes easier to read in bright light, and the app works for more people.
value.build-balance-assets: Builds the Asset register page, which lists your property, vehicles and valuables with what you paid, how fast they lose value and which policy insures each. It shows what you own beyond bank and investment accounts, and whether it is covered.
value.build-career-equity: Builds the Equity compensation page, which tracks your employer stock plans: when shares become yours or can be bought, the taxes they trigger and how concentrated you are. Stock pay can create surprise tax bills and put too much of your wealth in one company.
value.build-household-documents: Builds the Document vault index page, a list of where your will, insurance policies, deeds and tax returns are kept. It records locations only, not the files. If something happens to you, your family can find the right papers quickly.
value.build-household-life-events: Builds the Life events page, which walks you through a marriage, a baby, a job change, a move, an inheritance or a divorce and suggests the plan changes each one needs. Big events touch taxes, insurance and goals at once, and it is easy to miss one.
value.build-transactions-connect: Builds the Bank connections page, which links your banks through SimpleFIN or Plaid so new transactions arrive on their own, through the server on your PC. It saves the manual file download, but it lets an outside service see your bank data.
value.research-estate-inheritance-taxes: Builds a table of state estate and inheritance taxes for 2026, plus the federal exemption after the 2025 law, with sources and worked examples. The planned Estate tax page can then tell you whether your estate could owe tax. For most households the answer is no, but where it is yes the amounts are large.
value.build-career-side-income: Builds the Side income page, which models irregular income from gigs, freelance work or a small business so your plan counts it sensibly. Uneven income should not be treated like a steady paycheck, and this stops the plan from over-counting it.
value.build-goals-charitable: Builds the Giving page, which plans your charitable giving, works out the numbers for a donor-advised fund (an account you give into now and send to charities later) and shows how gifts affect your taxes. It helps you give what you intend while keeping the tax benefit.
value.build-property-purchase: Builds the Big purchase planner page, which helps you plan any large purchase: whether to save up or finance it, and what it does to your other goals. You see the trade-off before you commit.
value.research-529-deductions: Builds a state-by-state table of tax breaks for 529 college savings: deduction or credit, limits, carry-forward and what happens if you move money out, each with its source. The planned Education page can then count your state's tax saving. It matters only if you are saving for someone's education.
value.reasoning-spanish: Adds the machinery to show the app in Spanish (Mexico) and translates the menus, shared parts, the Dashboard and Settings. Other pages can follow the same pattern later. It matters if Spanish is easier for you or for family members who use the app.
value.build-ai-categorizer: Builds the Categoriser page, which sorts many transactions at once with the AI, shows how sure it is about each and gives you a table to check. It saves time on a first import, when hundreds of lines need a category.
value.build-balance-statement: Builds the Balance sheet page, a formal printable list of what you own and owe, split by owner and by how quickly each item turns into cash. Lenders, advisors and estate lawyers often ask for exactly this.
value.build-career-offer-compare: Builds the Job offer compare page, which compares the offers you have on total pay, including benefits and equity, not just salary. A higher salary can lose to a better retirement match or health plan.
value.build-estate-digital: Builds the Digital assets page, which records your online accounts, your password manager and where your crypto keys are kept, and who can get into each if something happens to you. Accounts nobody can open may be lost or locked for months.
value.build-investments-crypto: Builds the Crypto page, which tracks your crypto holdings and what you paid for them, with a clear flag on how much they swing in value. It keeps coins in your net worth and records the purchase prices you will need at tax time.
value.build-overview-benchmarks: Builds the How am I doing page, which compares your net worth, savings rate and debt load with households of a similar age and income. It gives a rough sense of whether you are ahead or behind, though every household is different and averages can mislead.
value.build-property-vehicles: Builds the Vehicles page, which works out what each vehicle really costs to own and whether to lease, buy or keep the one you have. Fuel, insurance, repairs and lost value add up to far more than the monthly payment.
value.build-reports-annual-review: Builds the Annual review pack page, which rolls your monthly reviews up into a single year-in-review. A yearly look back shows what progressed, what slipped and what to change next year.
value.build-taxes-documents: Builds the Tax documents checklist page, which lists the forms you need to collect each year and where each one comes from, such as your employer, bank or brokerage. Having everything in hand before you file avoids late corrections.
value.quick-doc-link-targets: Makes the links inside the in-app Docs pages (plan, catalog and notes) big enough to tap with a thumb. Today they are only 17 to 20 pixels tall, so on a phone you can miss them or open the wrong one. It affects only reading the project's own documents.
value.build-career-salary: Builds the Salary and raises page, which maps how your pay could grow with raises and promotions, shown in today's dollars. Future pay drives how much you can save, so a realistic path makes every projection more honest.
value.build-goals-travel: Builds the Travel and events page, which turns trips, a wedding or other milestones into goals you fund month by month. Saving ahead means you pay for them from savings instead of a credit card.
value.build-career-business: Builds the Small business page, which tracks your business's profit and loss, what you pay yourself and your self-employed retirement plans. It separates business money from household money so you can see your real take-home.
value.build-property-renovation: Builds the Renovation page, which weighs a renovation's cost against the value it adds to your home and how you would pay for it. It shows whether a project is worth doing before you borrow for it.
value.build-reports-statements: Builds the Financial statements page, which bundles your balance sheet, income statement and cash-flow statement into one printable pack. It is what lenders and advisors may ask for when you apply for credit or review your finances.
value.build-system-diagnostics: Builds the Diagnostics page, which shows on one page whether the server and the AI are working, the test results and the versions in use. When something stops working, you can see where the problem is.
value.quick-form-accessibility: Makes every form and green or red message in the app work with screen readers: each box is tied to its label, errors are announced and focus jumps to the first mistake. Nothing looks different. It matters if you or anyone using your planner relies on a screen reader.
value.build-household-contacts: Builds the Contacts page, one list of your advisor, accountant, attorney and insurers, with the last four digits of each account number. When you or your family need to call someone about money, you will not have to hunt for who and where.
value.build-property-rental: Builds the Rental analysis page, which works out a rental property's yield, cash return, whether the rent covers the loan, a vacancy allowance and depreciation. It shows you whether a property really makes money after all costs.
value.build-estate-gifting: Builds the Gifting page, which plans gifts within the yearly tax-free limit and shows how to front-load a 529 college plan with five years of gifts at once. It helps you give to family without using up your lifetime gift-tax exemption.
value.research-open-source-2026: Refreshes the list of open-source finance projects the planner learns from: which are still maintained, their licences, and which code can be reused legally in your MIT-licensed repo. It keeps borrowed ideas and code on safe legal ground, but changes nothing you see in the app.
value.build-estate-inheritance: Builds the Expected inheritance page, where you model money you might receive as a what-if scenario instead of counting on it in your main plan. You can see how much it would help without relying on it.
value.build-estate-estate-tax: Builds the Estate tax page, showing whether your estate could owe federal or state estate tax and how much of the exemption you have used. Most households are well under the federal limit, but a few states tax much smaller estates.
value.build-ai-notes: Builds the Voice notes page, which turns a spoken note into text and suggests entries from it for you to confirm. Saying 'paid the plumber four hundred dollars' is quicker than typing on a phone.
value.build-cashflow-statement: Builds the Cash-flow statement page, a printable report that groups your money movements into everyday living, investing and borrowing. It is the accountant's view of where cash came from and went, mostly useful when someone else asks for it.
value.build-career-human-capital: Builds the Human capital page, which puts a value on all the money you are still going to earn, which is what your insurance needs are based on. It shows why protecting your income matters most while much of your wealth is still ahead of you.
value.quick-shares-property-tests: Adds a stress test for the rounding that makes the 'Where it goes' percentages on Expenses add up to exactly 100, checking thousands of random lists. It protects a fix already made, so a later change cannot quietly bring back shares that add up to 101.
